facts.text: Conquest was Italy's answer to the hit Quest for Fire (1981). Director Lucio Fulci's film joined a wave of cavemen-and-sorcery cash-ins, like Umberto Lenzi's Ironmaster (1982).
Conquest's original Italian shooting title was Mace, il fuorilegge, or Mace, the Outlaw, naming the grumpy hero played by Jorge Rivero instead of the kid with the bow.
Spanish actress Violeta Cela, the sacrificial victim here, is a second niece of Nobel Prize-winning writer Camilo José Cela. She made her screen debut in 1978.
Conquest was a bomb in Italy. Film historian Roberto Curti says it grossed under 100 million lire. It did better in Mexico, where star Jorge Rivero was a big name.
Before Hollywood, Mexican star Jorge Rivero (Mace) was a bodybuilder and athlete with a chemical engineering degree. He later played opposite John Wayne in Rio Lobo (1970) and guested on Columbo.
The eye symbol on Mace's forehead matches the Book of Eibon symbol from director Lucio Fulci's earlier horror film The Beyond (1981), according to Schlockmania.
Actor José Gras, who plays Fado, says acting fully covered in fur as one of the wolfmen was a challenge. He adds the wolfman extras didn't bond much with the leads, per Mondo Digital.
Cinematographer Alejandro Ulloa used a fog machine, a soft-focus lens and special filters to give Conquest its hazy, dreamlike look.
Sabrina Siani (Ocron) was born Sabrina Seggiani and also billed as Sabrina Sellers. She made most of her films between 17 and 20, and retired from acting in 1989 at age 26.
Fulci was offered Conquest by producer Gianni Di Clemente while shooting Manhattan Baby in 1982. He signed a two-film deal, then left and never made the second movie.
The film shot in Mexico, Sardinia and Rome. It was an Italian-Spanish-Mexican co-production, and interiors were filmed at R.P.A. Elios Studios in Rome.
Schlockmania describes Claudio Simonetti's synth score as 'New Age on steroids.' Simonetti was a member of the Italian prog band Goblin, known for Suspiria and Dawn of the Dead.
For masked villain Ocron, Fulci judged actresses on their bodies only, since the mask hid the face. An investor sitting in on the auditions pushed him to cast Sabrina Siani.
Conrado San Martín, who plays the dark spirit Zora, made his film debut in 1941. He later appeared in Hollywood-scale epics like King of Kings (1961) and The Colossus of Rhodes (1961).
Composer Claudio Simonetti says he dealt only with the producers on Conquest and never discussed the music with director Lucio Fulci. It was an early solo job after his time in the band Goblin.
The Monthly Film Bulletin called Conquest a 'deliriously magpie mix of Conan the Barbarian, Quest for Fire and Raiders of the Lost Ark,' with a score it found 'wonderfully inappropriate.'
A reviewer at Good Efficient Butchery noticed some of Claudio Simonetti's synth cues here sound a lot like Fabio Frizzi's score for Lucio Fulci's City of the Living Dead (1980).
Anne Billson of London's Time Out noted the film's 'inordinate amount of spurting wounds, severed heads and oozing poison pustules,' plus orange-filtered skies.
For US audiences the stars were rebilled: Jorge Rivero became 'George Rivero' and Sabrina Siani became 'Sabrina Sellers'. United Film Distribution Company released it in spring 1984.
Jeremy Wheeler of AllMovie gave Conquest two stars out of five. He still called it a 'schlock masterpiece' for viewers with their tongues planted firmly in cheek.
UK censors cut 4 minutes 8 seconds from early video releases: nudity, bursting sores, a beheading and brain-eating. The Blue Underground DVD restored it all.
Bands About Movies compared villain Ocron's gold mask and near-nudity to G.I. Joe's Destro. Actress Sabrina Siani wears little else for the whole film.
Fulci reportedly left right after shooting Conquest, refusing to finish his contract with producer Giovanni Di Clemente after disagreements on set.
Richard Scheib of Moria called the crucifixion and dolphin-rescue sequence imaginative. He picked the cheap animated 'laser arrows' as the film's shoddiest effect.
Fulci said Conquest's low budget didn't hurt it. He believed its fog-covered lands and weird denizens would linger in viewers' minds as the work of an artist with a distinctive visual style.
Mondo Digital notes a wishbone disembowelment scene was cut from early US releases. The site also says Sabrina Siani is seen nude with a boa constrictor.
Fulci was a medical student and art critic before directing. Three of his films, Zombie, The Beyond and The House by the Cemetery, landed on the original UK 'video nasties' list.
Conquest hit US theaters in April 1984 at 89 minutes and the UK in May 1984 at 84 minutes. Mexico didn't get it until August 15, 1985.
Conquest gets a shout-out in George Romero's zombie film Day of the Dead (1985) and is spoofed in the anthology ABCs of Death 2 (2014).
Star Jorge Rivero emerged in the late 1960s as a Mexican leading man and sex symbol. He has appeared in more than 100 productions across Mexico, the US and Europe.
